advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `code_review_recall` and `code_review_no_fire` deterministic scorers to the eval spec (matching the packaged code-review overlay specs) so the RP-F/RP-N corpus actually gates, and update the test's scorer-name assertion.
evidence: Spec scorers block lists only one scorer: `name: code_review_emits_valid_findings` with `description: Fire cases emit schema-valid findings and pass cases emit none.` (.rebar/evals/...eval.yaml:9-11)

`_schema_code_review_findings` returns `ScoreResult(True, True)` whenever `out.get("findings")` is a list — it is applicable/passing for BOTH fire and pass cases and never inspects expect (src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_scorers.py:193-202)

Every packaged code-review overlay spec adds recall+no_fire gating scorers, e.g. code-review-security.eval.yaml:16-21 lists `code_review_recall` and `code_review_no_fire` alongside `code_review_emits_valid_findings`
`run_eval` gates only on the deterministic scorers named in the spec (src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:658-691); with just the shape scorer the RP-F/RP-N labels never gate
The test locks the single-scorer set: `assert [s["name"] for s in deterministic] == ["code_review_emits_valid_findings"]` (tests/unit/test_project_review_phase_boundaries.py)
advisory.finding: The eval spec's only deterministic (gating) scorer is `code_review_emits_valid_findings`, which merely checks the output carries a `findings` list; it never verifies that fire cases (RP-F1..6) actually fire or pass cases (RP-N1..6) produce no findings. The recall/no-fire discrimination the corpus was built for is therefore unenforced by the live `run_eval` gate, contradicting the scorer's own description.
scenarios: A future prompt edit that stops firing on any RP-F case (or false-fires on RP-N cases) still passes `rebar prompt eval code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries`, since the sole gating scorer is satisfied by any well-shaped output.
advisory.suggested_fix: In .rebar/evals/code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries.eval.yaml add two more deterministic scorers under `scorers:` — `code_review_recall` (fire cases must produce a finding) and `code_review_no_fire` (pass cases must not) — mirroring code-review-security.eval.yaml, and update the equality assertion in test_eval_spec_is_strict_balanced_and_uses_code_review_schema accordingly.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the prompt prose-marker greps in test_prompt_encodes_phase_ownership_and_abstention_guards with assertions on parsed/branched contract values (front-matter fields, schema id) or drop the wording checks.
evidence: for marker in ("grounded evidence", "severity", "confidence", "suggested_fix", "documentation", "negative example", "unchanged", "abstain", "unclear",): assert marker in body (lines 108-119)

The grepped tokens are free prose in .rebar/prompts/code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries.md (e.g. 'abstain when the owning phase is unclear' line 12-13, 'When in doubt, emit nothing' line 40) read only by the LLM, not a parser/validator — unlike prompt.category/prompt.dimension which ARE parsed front-matter and asserted at lines 102-103.
Rule-5 rescues instruction-artifact greps only when a non-human consumer branches on the exact value; an LLM is not a non-human consumer, so a prose-wording grep is a change-detector.
advisory.finding: test_prompt_encodes_phase_ownership_and_abstention_guards greps the Pass-1 prompt body for prose wording markers ('grounded evidence', 'abstain', 'unclear', 'documentation', 'negative example', 'unchanged') that no non-human consumer parses or branches on; a behavior-preserving reword of the rubric would break the test, making it a change-detector rather than a behavior/contract assertion.
scenarios: A rubric author rewords 'abstain' to 'do not emit' or reorders the Do-not-flag bullets with identical intent -> the test fails despite no observable behavior change.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a solver-path test exercising at least one RP-N pass diff (and asserting zero findings) alongside the RP-F fire case, so the fire/pass discrimination is regression-covered.
evidence: _RecordingRunner.run returns FakeRunner(structured={"findings": [finding]}).run(req) with a constant `finding` regardless of the input diff (lines 65-67).
run_case is invoked with only the RP-F1 fire diff; no RP-N* pass diff is exercised through any solver, and out["findings"] == [finding] (line 94) merely echoes the mock's configured return.
test_injected_perfect_solver keys its classifier off case["expect"] (line 175), so it exercises calibrate_criterion aggregation math but never the fire/pass discrimination.
Sibling test_eval_solver_project_criterion.py drives run_case AND asserts a pass path exists (dataset has T-F and T-N), showing the established pattern for exercising both classes.
advisory.finding: No offline test drives an actual solver over both a fire (RP-F*) and a pass (RP-N*) diff to verify the criterion distinguishes them; the only run_case test feeds a single fire diff through a runner whose run() returns a hardcoded findings list unconditionally, so a regression where the criterion fires on pass cases (or drops fire cases) would go undetected.
scenarios: A future rubric or routing change causes findings to surface on RP-N pass cases (false-accept) — the offline suite stays green because no pass diff is ever run through a solver.
